title: MonochromeBall
coverAlt: Black Mode reveals white platforms beside the ball in MonochromeBall Stage 2
description: One switch. Two modes. Four stages. A 3D puzzle platformer where changing color changes where you can land.
role: Solo developer · Gameplay and level design
overview: MonochromeBall explores a single rule across four stages. White Mode makes black platforms solid. Black Mode makes white platforms solid. Matching platforms disappear and lose collision, while neutral gray platforms stay solid in both modes.

contributions.title: Color and collision
contributions.text: I built the mode switch to update the camera background, ball, and platforms together. Invisible fan blades keep their colliders, so their motion still matters when their color blends into the background.

contributions.title: Movement and timing
contributions.text: I implemented ball movement, jumping, and a follow camera, then built platforms that travel vertically or change color after a delay. The camera angle and landing distances were refined through testing.

contributions.title: Four-stage progression
contributions.text: I designed the stages to teach movement and switching first, then use the same rule for falling, route finding, and timing jumps around moving platforms.

stages.name: Stage 1
stages.title: Learn the switch
stages.text: Start on safe gray platforms. Move, jump, and switch modes in midair to reach the next landing, then pass rotating obstacles.

stages.name: Stage 2
stages.title: Make the floor disappear
stages.text: Change modes to remove the platform under the ball and fall onto the route below. These captures show how the available platforms change between modes.

stages.name: Stage 3
stages.title: Read the route
stages.text: Reveal a route map in Black Mode. Timed platforms flip color after a delay and eventually reset, so the route depends on when you move as well as which mode you use.

stages.name: Stage 4
stages.title: Time the landing
stages.text: Cross rising and falling platforms, then judge gaps in rotating fans. Hidden blades remain solid, so switching modes changes what you can see while the fan keeps turning.
